questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

The old library had (1)___ shelves, (2)___ books and (3)___ corners, where students could study in peace, surrounded by historical knowledge.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes the old library with specific characteristics.
 
• The word "**towering**" is appropriate for shelves, as they are tall.
 
• The word "**dusty**" fits well for books, as old libraries often have books covered in dust.
 
• The word "**quiet**" is fitting for corners, as they provide peaceful spaces for studying.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The old library had towering__ shelves, __dusty__ books and __quiet__ corners, where students could study in peace, surrounded by historical knowledge.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Towering**: means very tall or high.
 
• **Dusty**: means covered with or resembling dust.
 
• **Quiet**: means making little or no noise; calm and peaceful.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

The hotel’s spacious rooms and convenient location ______________ for our family vacation perfectly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "fit the bill".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"fit the bill"** means to be suitable for a particular purpose or requirement; to meet the necessary conditions or criteria. (ज़रूरत को पूरा करना)

 
 
• **Example:** This software fits the bill perfectly for our business needs.
 
 
 
• **Explanation:** The spacious rooms and convenient location of the hotel were exactly what the family required for their vacation, making "fit the bill" the most appropriate choice. (ज़रूरत के अनुसार होना)
 
 
• **Example:** The new dress fit the bill for the wedding party.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Fit to be tied** (बहुत गुस्से में होना): Refers to being extremely angry or annoyed.

 
 
• **Example:** He was fit to be tied when he found out someone had scratched his car.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Fit of rage** (गुस्से का दौरा): Refers to a sudden burst of anger or fury.
 
 
• **Example:** In a fit of rage, he slammed the door and left the room.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Fit to kill** (बहुत आकर्षक या शानदार): Refers to being dressed or looking exceptionally stylish or impressive.
 
 
• **Example:** She was dressed to kill at the party and turned heads wherever she went.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the INCORRECT usage of adverb.

options.text: Nancy had completely forgotten about the meeting.
Thomas seldomly takes time off work, even when necessary.
The coffee tasted very bitter to him.
They will soon finish the project, despite the delays.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The incorrect usage of the adverb is in the phrase 'seldomly takes'.**

__
 
• **The word 'seldomly' is not standard English usage.**
 
• The correct word is **'seldom'**, which is an adverb that means 'not often' or 'rarely'.
 
 
• **For example -**
 
• Thomas seldom takes time off work, even when necessary.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **'seldomly takes' (Option 2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Let’s review the correct usage of adverbs in the other sentences:**

 
• **Option 1:** 'Completely forgotten' is correct. 'Completely' modifies 'forgotten' appropriately.
 
• **Option 3:** 'Very bitter' is correct. 'Very' is an intensifier modifying 'bitter'.
 
• **Option 4:** 'Will soon finish' is correct. 'Soon' modifies 'finish' appropriately.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• The other options: "**commended**" is similar but less specific, "**derided**" means mocked (which is inappropriate here), and "**approved**" does not convey the sense of public recognition as effectively.

**Complete Sentence:** *In the present situation, teachers not only face criticism, but are also applauded__ for their innovative teaching methodologies.*

• **Approved (मंजूरी देना)**: means officially agreed or accepted, but lacks the nuance of appreciation.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable collocation.

She ______________ asthma all her life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**has suffered from**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb phrase "**has suffered from**" is a correct collocation used to describe an ongoing or long-term condition.
 
• In this context, the sentence refers to a continuous state ("**all her life**"), which requires the present perfect tense "**has suffered from**."
 
• **Options 2, 3, and 4** are either grammatically incorrect or do not fit the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"She **has suffered from**__ asthma all her life."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "suffered to"** is incorrect because "suffer" is not followed by "to" in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "has suffered"** is incomplete as it does not specify what she suffered from.
 
• **Option 4: "is suffering in"** is incorrect because it is not the correct tense or preposition for this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**neutral**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage compares participants’ reactions when exposed to **gaming-related content** with their reactions to another type of content.
 
• The contrast indicates that the other type of content should be **neutral** or non-stimulating, to measure the difference in desire caused by gaming cues.
 
• Hence, “**neutral content**” appropriately fits the blank because it provides a balanced comparison in a psychological study context.
 
• Other options like “positivity,” “negativity,” and “gaming” do not fit logically since they either overlap or fail to contrast with gaming cues.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Positivity:** Refers to optimistic or encouraging content, which doesn’t contrast neutrally with gaming content.
 
• **Negativity:** Means discouraging or harmful content, which could influence mood rather than serve as a neutral baseline.
 
• **Gaming:** Repetition of the same type of content, which fails to create the required comparison in the experiment.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.

• The passage discusses the results of a study examining the relationship between psychological traits and gaming desire.
